newsitem.title: UK: UK shares close firm, but off record peak.
newsitem.headline: UK shares close firm, but off record peak.

text.p: UK shares ended higher on Friday, but well off their record peaks set earlier after an early burst of buying on Wall Street faded, dealers said.

Surging U.S. stocks propelled the benchmark FTSE 100 to a fresh record at 4,100 briefly before slowly giving back gains. The index ended 26.3 points higher at 4,077.6. Advancers led decliners 66 to 31.
The latest surge on Wall Street -- where the Dow rose by more than 70 points within the first 15 minutes of trading on the back of a 126-point jump overnight -- rippled across the Atlantic.
But just as the Dow eased off its highs, UK shares eased off theirs.
"The Dow carried us up and it carried us back down," said one dealer.
U.S. blue chips were up about 25 points when London markets closed.
"The Dow's jump overnight was unbelievable," said one senior dealer. "It certainly has given the market a boost of confidence."
Bid speculation swirled around UK dealings rooms added to the bullish mood, traders said.
Shares in General Accident added 9-1/2p to 759-1/2p after rising to a record of 779 on growing bid rumours that have propped up the insurance sector recently.

Thames Water and United Utilities shares rose as the flurry of takeover bids in the electricity sector spilled over into water stocks, dealers said. Thames finished 21p higher at 610p and United closed 13-1/2p higher at 607p.
Shares in Wolseley gained 12p to 459-1/2p after Credit Lyonnais Laing recommended the stock as a buy, along with other stocks in the building sector.
Credit Lyonnais Laing's Mike Foster said he saw momentum gathering in the building sector and a turnaround in sentiment.
But jitters about Christmas sales, prompted by an evening press report, knocked shares in Next and Marks & Spencer lower late in the session.
"It's been a very disappointing Christmas," said analyst Nick Bubb at Mees Pierson. "There will be a last minute rush, but it won't be enough to make up for it.
Shares in Next lost 7-1/2p to 544-1/2p, while shares in Marks & Spencer closed 11p lower at 473p.
Today's advance added another leg to the UK market's long-awaited year-end rally, usually attributed to seasonal inflows of cash into investment fund coffers.

And with a recent spate of takeover bids promising to inject further cash into the market, as well as prompting further gains in other possible bid targets, some traders and analysts said the FTSE could push towards 4,200 before the year is out.
Yet major uncertainties remained over the outlook for 1997.
Signs that UK economic growth is gaining pace are expected to force Chancellor Kenneth Clarke to raise interest rates in the first quarter of the new year.

And with Prime Minister John Major's parliamentary majority already wiped out, concern is likely to grow over the timing of the general election which must be held by May 22 and which the opposition Labour Party is well placed to win.
"All those uncertainties may well create a period of consolidation at the start of 1997," said the head of equity trading at one brokerage.
